fix_note: Saving a board no longer sends its update ping to every connected user — the ping now goes only to the board owner's session, the way the board's own live-editing events already travel room-by-room (per-user notification scoping, as in Slack/Notion). Private boards stay private in the realtime layer too.

Choosing Private (or Followers) in the post composer now actually sets the post's audience — before, every post was stored public no matter what was picked, even though the feed already enforced private/followers visibility on read (Facebook-style audience selector: the choice is honored, and the post itself shows its audience). The composer also resets to Public after each post, so a one-off private post no longer leaves the selector stuck on Private, and your own non-public posts carry a Private/Followers badge in the Social home feed.

Events now record a visibility when created (Private by default, Public on request — the Google Calendar / Eventbrite create-time choice), the planner offers the control in the create form and on the event itself, event lists show Private/Public and whether the public page is live, and publishing a public page for a private event is refused with a plain explanation instead of silently going public. Verified end to end on the real domain code: default private, publish refused while private, unpublish always allowed, publish succeeds after flipping to Public, junk values fall back to private.

A council member can now prepare a proposal privately: drafts are visible to their author alone — other members' proposal lists no longer include them, a draft can't be found or voted on by anyone else, and the shared audit trail records the creation without the draft's title. Moving the proposal out of Draft (to Discussion) shares it with the council exactly as before, and the chamber already labels the author's own drafts as Draft. Verified on the real domain code with two members: draft hidden from the second member end to end, then visible and votable after the author published it.

The Household lens badge no longer says 'Real but static / open-access dataset' over a family's own records. That wording described only the lens's reference content; the badge caption now names both halves — reference content (seasonal checklists, maintenance schedules) is real and from open sources, and the household's own records (members, meal plans, chores, budgets) are the member's alone, saved privately on their account. Done as a household entry in the shared depth-badge override table, the same mechanism other lenses use when the generic caption misdescribes them.
